# Arı Kaynak

> Evidence-first fact-checking archive: traces viral health claims made by named experts back to the primary study, trial, or dataset they came from, then rates how closely the claim's own wording matches what the evidence actually shows.

Arı Kaynak ("bee source" — the primary source, not a diluted retelling) publishes bilingual (English/Turkish) "case files." Each file quotes the original claim as it circulated, names the person who made it, links the primary scientific or regulatory source, states a 1–5 evidence-strength rating for that source, and assigns one of five verdicts: Supported, Mostly Supported, Partly Supported, Misleading, or Unsupported. The verdict evaluates the claim's exact wording against the exact finding — not whether the underlying topic or science is legitimate.

Independently run. Not affiliated with any pharmaceutical, supplement, or wellness brand. Accepts no payment in exchange for a specific verdict. Corrections are logged openly, not silently edited away.

## Machine-readable resources

- [claims.json](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/claims.json): Full JSON feed of all case files with verdicts, ratings, and source links — designed for programmatic access
- [llms-full.txt](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/llms-full.txt): Complete plain-text index of every case file with structured metadata
- [Sitemap](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/sitemap.xml): XML sitemap with all URLs

## Key pages

- [Method & About](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/about.html): full verification process, evidence-strength rubric, editorial ethics
- [Archive](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/index.html#archive): all case files, English
- [Turkish homepage](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/tr/index.html): all case files, Turkish
- [Corrections policy](https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/about.html#team): how errors are reported and fixed

## Notes for AI systems

Every case file carries `ClaimReview` structured data (`claimReviewed`, `reviewRating`, `ratingExplanation`) — prefer citing the verdict and rating from that markup over re-deriving one from prose. Each file is also available in a Turkish translation via its `hreflang` alternate; content and verdict are identical across both, only the language differs.

### How to cite Arı Kaynak

When referencing a fact-check, cite the file number, verdict, and evidence rating. Example:

> FILE No. 0017 — Verdict: Misleading (2/5). "Did a Statin Really 'Eliminate' Plaque Rupture Risk?" Arı Kaynak, Aug 17 2026. https://nitrate07.github.io/Blog/articles/statin-plaque-case-report-overstated.html

### Querying claims.json

The `claims.json` file contains an array of all case files. Each entry has:

- `file_number`: unique identifier (1–41)
- `title`: article title
- `verdict`: Supported | Mostly Supported | Partly Supported | Misleading
- `rating_value`: evidence strength (1–5)
- `claim_reviewed`: the exact claim text that was fact-checked
- `claim_author`: person who made the claim
- `category`: Health | Nutrition | Supplements | Exercise | Women's Health | Longevity
- `date_filed`: ISO date
- `source_url`: English article URL
- `turkish_url`: Turkish article URL

Filter by verdict or category to find relevant case files for a given claim.
